appraisal_events.evidence: At Mme de Guise's villa the duchess is "plus qu'une invitée pareille aux autres, et par là plus émouvante encore pour moi, plus elle-même"; the closing image of her descending in her flesh-satin dress, "comme dans une coquille, entre ces valves glacées de nacre rose," is said to hold "tous les plaisirs du faubourg Saint-Germain."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's fascinated admiration for the duchess deepens: paradoxically, seeing her reduced to an ordinary guest among princesses makes her more moving and more essentially herself to him, and her radiant appearance condenses the whole enchantment of the Faubourg Saint-Germain.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's private aesthetic rapture elevates her further in his own estimation, though this remains his own admiration rather than a publicly witnessed status shift.
